about: The worked SAQ essays on anantf.com/exams (PDFs in its exams/reference/), for qbank/tools/import-exams.mjs. plan: the essay is also in the study plan, so that question gets the link instead of a new one (the start of its case text). Otherwise stem is the question as written in the PDF, typed out here once.

essays.title: Difficult extubation
essays.stem: Outline extubation strategies for anticipated difficult extubation of an adult.

essays.title: Frailty & prehabilitation
essays.stem: Define frailty and discuss the role of prehabilitation for patients with frailty.

essays.title: Pneumoperitoneum & steep Trendelenburg
essays.stem:
You are providing anaesthetic care for a 65 year old male, who weighs 98 kg, with a height of 170 cm. He has hypertension and is a heavy smoker (20 pack-years).

A. Outline the physiological response to the establishment of pneumoperitoneum and subsequent steep Trendelenburg positioning (50%).
B. You observe a steady increase in his end-tidal carbon dioxide tension, from 35 to 70 mmHg, during the first hour of anaesthesia with an associated increase in heart rate to 110 bpm. Describe your assessment (50%) and management (50%).

essays.title: Anaesthetic machine safety
essays.stem: Describe the safety features of anaesthetic workstation in preventing delivery of hypoxic mixture.

essays.title: High-flow nasal cannula
essays.stem:
A. Describe the physiological effects of a high-flow nasal cannula device (HFNC), e.g. Optiflow or Airvo (30%).
B. Briefly list the indications, and justify its use in an adult endoscopy suite (70%).

essays.title: HOCM for laparoscopic cholecystectomy
essays.stem:
A 40 year old man with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) presents for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

A. Describe the principles of intraoperative haemodynamic management for this patient (40%).
B. How would you manage hypotension post induction of general anaesthesia in this patient? (60%)

essays.title: Brainstem death & organ donation
essays.stem: Outline the clinical criteria for diagnosis of brainstem death. Outline the physiological implications of brain stem death following SAH in a patient listed for organ donation.

essays.title: SCI — laparotomy 10 days post C6 transection
essays.stem:
A 40-year-old requires a laparotomy 10 days after an isolated traumatic spinal cord transection at C6.

A. Outline the key anaesthetic issues (50%).
B. How would these influence your anaesthetic management? (50%)

essays.title: Post-operative hypoxaemia in PACU
essays.stem: You have been asked to see a previously well 64-year-old man in the PACU with SpO2 of 85% two hours after laparoscopic right partial nephrectomy during which he lost 1 litre of blood. List the likely causes of the desaturation and outline your approach to managing the patient’s hypoxaemia.

essays.title: Fontan circulation in pregnancy
essays.stem: A 25-year-old woman who is 30 weeks pregnant has been referred to your tertiary high-risk obstetric clinic. She has complex cyanotic congenital heart disease and now functions with a Fontan circulation. How would you stratify the cardiovascular risk? What are the issues relevant to anaesthetic care that will need to be managed for this patient?

essays.title: Myotonic dystrophy for appendicectomy
essays.stem: A 30-year-old patient with myotonic dystrophy is scheduled for surgery for acute appendicitis. Outline your anaesthetic considerations.

essays.title: Paediatric penetrating eye injury
essays.stem: Discuss your approach to the anaesthetic management of a screaming 5-year-old child with penetrating eye injury.

essays.title: Perioperative hypertension
essays.stem: A patient presents on the day of surgery with a blood pressure of 180/110mmHg. Justify your decision to proceed with or postpone surgery for this patient.

essays.title: Fixed-ratio vs goal-directed transfusion
essays.stem: Discuss fixed ratio blood product transfusion versus goal directed factor concentrate administration in the management of a severely injured polytrauma patient.

essays.title: RA for total knee replacement
essays.stem:
A 60-year-old woman is scheduled for a right total knee replacement for severe osteoarthritis under general anaesthesia.

A. Discuss the role of regional anaesthesia (RA) techniques for intraoperative and postoperative analgesia in this patient (50%).

essays.title: Pain management for open liver resection
essays.stem:
A. List the methods of analgesia that can be used for patients undergoing open liver resection surgery (30%).
B. Justify your perioperative pain management strategy (70%).

essays.title: TEVAR for acute thoracic dissection
essays.stem:
A 75-year-old man presents with an acute dissection of the descending thoracic aorta. His blood pressure measures 190/110 mmHg.

A. Justify your plan for his preoperative blood pressure management (30%).
B. Describe the potential complications of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) and how you would mitigate them (70%).

essays.title: EVAR — anaesthetic concerns & MAC
essays.stem:
A. Outline the anaesthetic concerns associated with elective endovascular repair of infra-renal abdominal aortic aneurysm (EVAR) (50%).
B. Discuss the factors favouring monitored anaesthesia care (MAC) as the choice of anaesthesia for EVAR (50%).

essays.title: Cerebellar AVM in pregnancy — LSCS
essays.stem:
A 35-year-old woman at 32 weeks of pregnancy presents for Caesarean section under general anaesthesia. She was diagnosed with a cerebellar arteriovenous malformation (AVM) at 16 weeks. At 28 weeks there was bleeding from AVM rupture, which was managed conservatively. She is planned for early endovascular embolisation after the delivery.

A. How are you going to prepare this patient for the Caesarean section? (30%)
B. Describe how you would conduct your anaesthesia (30%).
The surgery finished in one hour but the patient failed to wake up.
C. What are the causes and how are you going to approach this problem? (40%)

essays.title: NMBA — residual block & avoidance
essays.stem:
A. List the ways to assess a patient for the presence of residual neuromuscular blockade (30%).
B. Discuss methods to reduce the risk of residual neuromuscular blockade (70%).

essays.title: Hip fracture — RA & postoperative delirium
essays.stem:
An 85-year-old woman is scheduled for hemiarthroplasty for a neck of femur fracture sustained after a fall. She has a background history of Alzheimer’s dementia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus and ischaemic heart disease.

A. Outline the innervation of the hip (20%).
B. Compare and contrast the use of a femoral nerve block with fascia iliaca block for analgesia in this patient (30%).
C. Justify strategies used to mitigate post-operative delirium in this patient (50%).
